meta.description: Percentile tables to map 1-99 player attributes to physical values (DFL)
meta.source: DFL/Sportec open data: Bassek, M., Rein, R., Weber, H., Memmert, D. (2025). An integrated dataset of spatiotemporal and event data in elite soccer. Scientific Data 12:195. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04505-y. Licence: CC-BY 4.0. Aggregate statistics only; no raw, frame-level or person-level data.
meta.licence: CC-BY 4.0 (data); these aggregates are derived statistics with attribution

config.xg_angle_slope_source: Soccermatics angle-only logistic fit, logit(xG) = -3.52 + 2.84 * theta, on 8,451 shots of the 2017/18 Premier League in the open Wyscout data (Pappalardo et al. 2019, Scientific Data 6:236, doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0247-7, CC BY 4.0)

conventions.coordinates: metres, centre origin, team-attacking direction: the team attacks +x, left is +y; pitch 105 x 68 m
conventions.validity: valid samples only (valid_kinematics = true); estimated gap samples never count for speed, peaks or per-90 values
conventions.per90: normalised on measured (valid) time of each player-match (team decision 2026-10-24); see coverage
conventions.ball: ball status and possession are the provider's (never derived from a stationary ball)

notes: Privacy (v4.2, team decision 2026-10-25): each table stores only the 21 quantiles at quantile_levels_pct (p2.5, p5, p10, ..., p90, p95, p97.5; linear interpolation of the per-player-match metric), with no minimum and no maximum, as realism_reference.json. values[k-1] (k = 1..99, the format the generator reads) is interpolated linearly from those quantiles at level k, flat below p2.5 and above p97.5 (attributes 1-2 equal p2.5, 98-99 equal p97.5). Known limit, accepted (guidelines section 19; CC-BY aggregates): with linear interpolation a stored quantile can coincide with one player-match value, when its position p x (n - 1) / 100 is a whole number (for example the median of an odd n). A 1-99 attribute k maps to values[k-1]; use insidethegame_data.calibration.attribute_to_value / value_to_attribute (clipped to 1..99).

pace, acceleration, stamina, work_rate: player-matches with >= 60 valid minutes (as in physical_profiles.json). passing: player-matches with >= 20 located open-play passes. shot_power: per confirmed open-play shot without headers (as ball.json shot_speed_ms), overall only.

Tables need n >= 5; missing (null): ['pace/CM', 'acceleration/CM', 'stamina/CM', 'work_rate/CM', 'passing/CM', 'passing/ST']. Small tables (n < 15), coarse percentiles: ['pace/GK: n=12', 'pace/AM: n=9', 'acceleration/GK: n=12', 'acceleration/AM: n=9', 'stamina/GK: n=12', 'stamina/AM: n=9', 'work_rate/GK: n=12', 'work_rate/AM: n=9', 'passing/GK: n=11', 'passing/AM: n=5', 'passing/W: n=10'].
With 6 matches the tails are coarse on purpose: between stored levels the values are linear, and the extremes are flat.

pace.metric: top speed: maximum of our valid speed per player-match

acceleration.metric: peak positive tangential acceleration on valid samples per player-match

work_rate.metric: distance above 20 km/h per 90 per player-match

passing.metric: pass success share (next touch by a team-mate) per player-match with >= 20 located passes

shot_power.metric: peak valid ball speed in the 0.5 s after the kick of a confirmed open-play shot, headers excluded (per shot)
